evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance multi_PreOrder `(R : crelation X) : PreOrder (multi R). — over `Inductive multi `(R : crelation X) : crelation X := | multi_refl (x : X) : multi x x | multi_step (x y z : X) : R x y → multi y z → multi x z` (line 46), so `multi R v w` IS the type of paths from v to w in the graph whose edge set from v to w is `R v w`: `multi_refl` is the length-0 path and `multi_step` prepends one arrow. The instance asserts exactly the Remark's two clauses, its transitivity obligation discharged by `multi_trans` (line 62: `multi R x y → multi R y z → multi R x z`, proved by induction, i.e. path concatenation).

#[export] Program Instance hom_preorder {C : Category} : PreOrder (@hom C) := { PreOrder_Reflexive := fun _ => id; PreOrder_Transitive := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f }. — the second route to the Remark: reflexivity witnessed by the identity (the length-0 path) and transitivity by composition (concatenation); instantiated at the path category below it gives `v ≤ w iff there is a path v → w` verbatim.

Program Definition FreeOnQuiver : Category@{o h p} := {| obj := @nodes G; hom := tlist edges; homset := fun i j => {| equiv := tlist_quiver_equiv _ _ _ |}; id := fun _ => tnil; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g +++ f |}. — over `Class Quiver := { nodes : Type; edges : nodes → nodes → uedges; edgeset : ∀ X Y, Setoid (edges X Y) }` (line 54), the library's own graph notion; the morphisms are the finite composable paths, the identity is the length-0 path `tnil`, and composition is path concatenation, so the underlying preorder of this category (via hom_preorder) is the vertex set ordered by existence of a path.

statement_record.book: Every graph presents a preorder, and a Hasse diagram is exactly such a presentation: take the vertex set V as the underlying set and put v ≤ w iff the graph contains a path from v to w. Reflexivity holds by the length-0 path at each vertex; transitivity holds because a path u→v and a path v→w concatenate.
statement_record.intree: multi_PreOrder : PreOrder (multi R), where multi R is the inductively generated path relation on the graph with edge sets R v w (multi_refl = the length-0 path, multi_step = prepend an arrow, multi_trans = concatenation); equivalently FreeOnQuiver G is the category of paths of a Quiver (hom := tlist edges, id := tnil, compose := concatenation) and hom_preorder makes any category's hom relation a preorder with id for reflexivity and ∘ for transitivity.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Two disclosures, neither a gap in the Remark's claim: (i) intree-stronger/proof-relevant — `multi R` and `tlist edges` are the actual SETS of paths rather than the mere existence claim `∃ path`, and the truncation to a thin relation is exactly Proset's trivial hom-setoid (Instance/Proset.v:33, `equiv := fun _ _ => True`); (ii) the two routes do not compose verbatim, since Instance/Proset.v's `Proset` takes a Prop-valued `relation` while `multi R` is a Type-valued crelation, so building the thin CATEGORY of the closure would need a truncated closure — the Remark itself only claims a preorder, which multi_PreOrder gives. Hasse diagrams as pictures are nowhere formalized (grep -i hasse: 0 hits), but that clause of the Remark is a drawing convention, not mathematical content.

statement_record.book: A total order is a preorder additionally satisfying, for all x and y, that x ≤ y or y ≤ x. Two elements of a preorder are comparable when x ≤ y or y ≤ x holds; so a total order is exactly a preorder in which every two elements are comparable.

Definition Opposite `(C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := fun x y => @hom C y x; homset := fun x y => @homset C y x; id := @id C; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f; ... |}. — the example's third ordering: the hom relation is flipped while reflexivity and transitivity are re-derived, so `LessThanEqualTo_Category^op` is the reverse of the usual order on ℕ (5 ≤ 3), and by construction C^op^op = C on the nose.

statement_record.book: The naturals with their usual size ordering form a preorder that is moreover a TOTAL order (for all m, n either m ≤ n or n ≤ m), with a linear Hasse diagram — unlike the partition diagram (1.5), whose middle row has incomparable elements. One set carries many orders: the discrete ordering (n ≤ m only if n = m), the reverse of the usual ordering (5 ≤ 3), and the divisibility ordering (n ≤ m iff n divides m, so 2 ≤ 4 but not 2 ≤ 3).

evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance iso_equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphism := { Equivalence_Reflexive := @iso_id; Equivalence_Symmetric := @iso_sym; Equivalence_Transitive := fun _ _ _ g f => iso_compose f g }. — the example's first clause in full generality: in a thin category (a preorder, Instance/Proset.v:33, whose hom-setoid is `fun _ _ => True` so both iso laws hold vacuously) `x ≅ y` is exactly the book's 'x ≤ y and y ≤ x', and this instance asserts that relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. It is packaged as a setoid on objects by `ob_setoid : Setoid C := {| equiv := Isomorphism; setoid_equiv := iso_equivalence |}` (line 195).

Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u). — over the factorization preorder `sub_le u v := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }` with `sub_le_refl` (62) and `sub_le_trans` (67): a concrete in-tree preorder whose induced 'x ≤ y and y ≤ x' relation is proved to coincide with the setoid equality of SubObj (whose reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity are discharged in SubObj_Setoid, line 33) — the example's construction carried out on a real preorder.

Lemma components_resp {X : Type} (h : Fin.t N → X) (edges : list (Fin.t N * Fin.t N)) (l : Fin.t N → Fin.t N) : (∀ e, In e edges → h (fst e) = h (snd e)) → (∀ p, h (l p) = h p) → ∀ p, h (components edges l p) = h p. — with `po_apex := fin_countP po_isrep` (406, the number of classes), `po_cls p := fin_rank po_isrep (po_lab p) ...` (420, the class map) and `po_cls_rep (k : Fin.t po_apex) : po_cls (fin_select po_isrep k) = k` (445, a section, hence surjectivity of the class map), this is the passage 'equivalence relation ⇒ partition' realized concretely and computably for a finite carrier: the classes are indexed by a set, every element has a class, every class is hit, and any map respecting the relation factors through the classes.

statement_record.book: Every preorder induces a partition of its underlying set: the relation 'x ≤ y and y ≤ x' is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and Proposition 1.19 turns it into a partition of P. This illustrates the phrase 'A induces B' — a canonical automatic passage from an A to a B — and is drawn as an eight-element preorder alongside its four equivalence classes.
statement_record.intree: iso_equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphism (in a thin category, the symmetrization of ≤ is an equivalence relation), packaged as ob_setoid : Setoid C; sub_equiv_iff_mutual identifies that induced equivalence with the setoid equality on subobjects for the concrete factorization preorder; components_resp/po_cls/po_cls_rep exhibit the class map, class count and factorization property for a finite carrier.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the first clause (the induced relation is proved an equivalence, in any category, hence in any preorder, and is even the library's canonical notion of sameness of objects), intree-weaker for the second: the passage to a PARTITION exists only for finite carriers presented by an edge list, never as a general construction from a preorder.

gap: The general 'induces a partition' step is missing in two ways. (1) There is no set of equivalence classes / quotient set for a general equivalence relation (Prop 1.19 has no in-tree counterpart; grep 'partition' finds only Theory/Coq/List.v:391's list filter, and Lib/Setoid.v:18 explicitly says setoids 'stand in for quotient sets', i.e. the library carries the relation and never forms the classes). evidence.intree_statement: Lemma sub_le_trans (u v w : SubObj x) : sub_le u v → sub_le v w → sub_le u w. — with `sub_le u v := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }` (59) and `sub_le_refl (u : SubObj x) : sub_le u u` (62): the subsets of a fixed ambient object, ordered by inclusion (factorization of one mono through the other), form a preorder — the example's 'ordered by inclusion of subsets' clause, and by sub_le_unique (78) the inclusion witness is unique, so the order is thin as a preorder must be.

Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}. — the example's 'the power set is the set of ALL subsets of X' clause: the subsets of x correspond bijectively to the points of the power object, `Pow a := Ω ^ a` (Structure/Topos.v:129), whose defining role is exactly to internalize that collection (extended to relations by `relations_iso : SubObj (a × b) ≅ (a ~> Pow b)`, Structure/Topos.v:146).

Example FinSet_Pow_two : @Pow FinSet FinSet_Topos 2%nat = 4%nat := eq_refl. — in skeletal FinSet objects ARE cardinalities, so this asserts computably that the power set of a two-element set has four elements; `FinSet_Pow_membership` (line 89) evaluates the membership map `eval : Pow 2 × 2 ~> Ω` on a concrete subset code, so the elements of the power object really are subsets.

statement_record.book: For a set X the power set is the set of all subsets of X, given the order by inclusion of subsets — the order always intended when the power set is regarded as an ordered set. For a three-element set the Hasse diagram is a 3-cube; in general the power set of an n-element set has an n-dimensional cube as its Hasse diagram.
statement_record.intree: sub_le / sub_le_refl / sub_le_trans (the subsets of an ambient object under inclusion form a preorder, with unique inclusion witnesses); classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) with Pow a := Ω^a (the collection of all subsets, internalized); FinSet_Pow_two : Pow 2 = 4 (the count, computably).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on the 'all subsets' clause (a proven bijection with predicates in any elementary topos, plus a computing finite model) but intree-weaker on the ORDER clause: inclusion is a preorder on the external setoid SubObj x, and nothing transports it to the internal power object Pow a, so 'the power set regarded as an ORDERED set' is only half realized.

gap: Three shortfalls. (1) The order and the power object are never joined: `classifier_classifies` is an isomorphism of SETOIDS in Sets, order-forgetting, and no internal order on `Pow a` (no internal ⊆ : Pow a × Pow a ~> Ω) is defined, so the example's 'this is the order always intended when the power set is regarded as an ordered set' is unavailable at the power object. (2) `sub_le` is never packaged as an ordered object: no `Proset`/`Poset` instance is built from sub_le_refl/sub_le_trans (grep Proset/Poset: only nat and a bespoke two-element carrier), and there are no meets or joins of subobjects (grep 'intersect|union|lattice|meet|join' about subobjects: prose only, e.g. Structure/Pullback.v:94 calls a pullback of subobjects 'the intersection' without defining it). (3) TRAP: Instance/Ens.v:56 `EnsT (T : Type)` does have ALL subsets of a fixed carrier as its objects (`obj := Ensemble T`), which looks like the power set as a category — but its homs are `∃ f : T → T, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ f⁻¹ B`, i.e. preimage equalities under endofunctions of T, not inclusions, and it is not thin, so EnsT is NOT (P(T), ⊆). Finally the n-cube Hasse diagram has no counterpart (grep -i 'hasse|cube': no hits for Hasse; 'cube' only little-n-cubes operads).
